desc: Compute prefix sum arrays for both `nums` and `cost` to allow O(1) range sum queries.
Initialize a DP array `dp` of size `n + 1` where `dp[0] = 0` and all other values are infinity.
Iterate `i` from 1 to `n` (representing the end of the current partition) to fill the DP table.
Inside the loop, iterate `j` from `i-1` down to 0 to consider all possible previous partitions ending at `j`.

For each `j`, calculate the cost of the subarray `nums[j:i]` using the formula `(prefix_nums[i] - prefix_nums[j] + k * current_subarray_index) * (prefix_cost[i] - prefix_cost[j])`, where `current_subarray_index` is derived from the number of elements processed so far.
Update `dp[i]` with the minimum value found across all valid `j`.

Implement the `Solution` class with the `minimumCost` method using the Convex Hull Trick (CHT) optimization. This involves precomputing prefix sums, initializing the DP array, and then iterating through the number of subarrays `c` from 1 to `n`. For each `c`, maintain a deque of lines representing the previous DP layer to efficiently find the minimum cost transition in O(N) time per layer.
Implement the `minimumCost` method with the described logic.

Verify the implementation logic against the provided code, specifically checking the CHT line addition timing and the query logic to ensure correctness for the "partition into subarrays" problem where the subarray index `i` increments with each new segment.
Run the provided solution against the example cases to verify correctness.
Test edge cases: `n=1`, all `nums` and `cost` equal to 1, large values for `k`.
If tests pass, mark as solved.
